# Dillon OS Daily Intelligence Report
**Period:** 2026-08-04T01:31:25.458Z → 2026-08-05T07:31:25.458Z

## 1. Executive pulse
Low-to-moderate signal volume in the window. Primary developments center on the recent (July 28) MCP 2026-07-28 spec going fully live in ecosystem discussion—stateless core for better HTTP scalability, routing, and auth hardening—plus two high-visibility agent skills: Archify (verifiable architecture diagrams) and claude-seo (comprehensive SEO/AEO/GEO audits). Security caution around MCP servers and skill footers remains active. Sparse consumer/demographic or pure design-system drops; coding-efficiency and AEO tooling dominate.[1](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/)

**Observed vs. inference:** Evidence is mostly maintainer posts, GitHub READMEs, and low-engagement X shares. Freshness high for discussions of the July MCP release; Archify changelog notes activity into early August. No major official Cursor/Copilot/Claude Code core releases in-window.

## 2. High-signal findings
- **MCP 2026-07-28 spec (stateless core):** Official blog confirms removal of sessions/handshake, self-contained requests, header-based routing (Mcp-Method/Mcp-Name), cacheable lists, Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR), Tasks as extension, auth hardening (RFC 9207, deprecation of DCR toward CIMD), and 12-month deprecation windows. Tier-1 SDKs updated; ecosystem (Cloudflare, AWS, Microsoft, Figma, etc.) signaling day-zero or rapid support. Discussed actively on X as infrastructure win for remote/scaled servers, though application state still needs explicit handling.[1](https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/)[2](https://x.com/HOSAIF_hz/status/2084877830048063811)
- **Archify skill (tt-a1i/archify):** Agent skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc. Generates validated, interactive HTML architecture/workflow/sequence/data-flow/lifecycle diagrams from repo or description. Self-validates (schema/layout/route checks) before delivery; supports deltas for PR review, source-line tracing, exports (PNG/SVG/WebM/share cards). MIT, ~9k stars, recent stable v2.13.0 (changelog ~Aug 3). Install via `npx skills add`. Strong for repo navigation and handoff.[3](https://x.com/NainsiDwiv50980/status/2084903496868913453)[4](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify)
- **claude-seo (AgriciDaniel/claude-seo):** Universal skill for Claude Code with 25 sub-skills + 18 sub-agents covering technical SEO, E-E-A-T, schema, GEO/AEO, local/maps, clustering, e-comm, international, reporting. Parallel agents, falsifiable recs grounded in Google guidance. High stars (~11-12k range historically); optional paid extensions. Reddit/X notes undisclosed self-promo footer in outputs (community link)—source quality caution. Last notable commits mid-late July.[5](https://x.com/PythonHub/status/2084901099408850986)[6](https://github.com/AgricIDaniel/claude-seo)
- **Other:** Mentions of custom MCP servers, background menu-bar agent runners reusing Claude/Codex MCP configs, GlobalGPT image gen via MCP in Codex, security audits flagging MCP secret/install-hook risks, Orca (parallel sandboxed agents + per-workflow MCP), UX Pilot (AI wireframe-to-hi-fi + Figma/code + MCP interface). Low engagement overall.[7](https://x.com/CoolAssPuppy/status/2084897663007301721)[8](https://x.com/get_sigil/status/2084867088674369884)[9](https://x.com/orcaonsol_fun/status/2084865290572017813)

**Uncertainty:** Exact star counts and install volumes fluctuate; some X posts are promotional. Conflicting views on whether “just give terminal + curl” still beats structured MCP/skills for flexibility.

## 3. Consumer taste and demographic signals
Sparse direct signals in the 30-hour window. One observation of high visual taste clashing with pervasive “AI slop” in local banners, menus, and posters—suggests fatigue with generic AI aesthetics among design-aware consumers.[10](https://x.com/thieerrr/status/2084905160212636110)

**Inference (low confidence):** Reinforces need for real-image art direction, non-generic typography/layout, and vertical-specific craft in local-service sites to differentiate. No strong demographic, creator, or buying-language data; no conflicting evidence. Broader cultural push against probabilistic/AI-generated visuals may favor deterministic QA and maker-checker human review.

## 4. Agent, MCP, skill, GitHub, and workflow opportunities
- **MCP stateless migration:** Improves scalability for remote servers, load-balancing, and gateway routing. Compatible with existing stacks if clients/servers update; explicit state handles replace sessions. Governance (auth scopes, versioning) becomes the new bottleneck.[11](https://x.com/AleksejAros/status/2084903648740438157)
- **Archify:** High fit for repository navigation, planning/handoff, code review (architecture deltas), and documentation. Low context cost once installed; deterministic validation gates reduce hallucination risk. Overlap with existing diagram tools minimal due to agent-native + validation.
- **claude-seo:** Direct AEO/GEO/local SEO coverage useful for site factory and client audits. Parallel sub-agents for efficiency. Risk: promo footer and potential prompt-injection via skill instructions; secret handling via optional APIs (DataForSEO etc.) needs sandbox.
- **Coding loops:** Mentions of supervisory/parallel agents (Orca-style MCP per-workflow), Playwright integration tests, image gen via MCP. Security tools emphasizing quarantine-first for MCP packages.
- **Assessment criteria applied:** Prefer official repos/changelogs. Archify scores high on maintenance, MIT, validation, low monetary cost. claude-seo high capability but footer/permissions risk → sandbox only. No new Copilot/Cursor core plugins of note. Reject unmaintained or high-secret-exposure items.

**Classification preview:** Archify → sandbox-test; claude-seo → watch/sandbox with audit; MCP spec → watch/integrate (client-side); pure hype runners → reject or save-to-library.

## 5. Website factory, design, AEO, and retention implications
- **AEO/GEO/local:** claude-seo’s maps intelligence, schema, E-E-A-T, and AI-citability checks align with 25-site factory needs (source-ready FAQs, trust gates, Maps-to-site parity). Use for deterministic acceptance on audits.
- **Design/UI craft:** Archify for system maps in handoffs; UX Pilot for rapid wireframe-to-Figma/code (avoids pure generic AI look via iteration). Emphasize real imagery, tokens, responsive/a11y/performance gates over vibe-only generation. Storybook mentions remain aspirational.
- **Factory ops:** Parallel agent loops + validation (Archify-style) for maker-checker and independent visual critique. Stateless MCP eases preview/Netlify deploys of tool servers. Security alarms reinforce safe preview, secret isolation, and rollback.
- **Retention/CRO:** Limited new signals; focus on third-visit behavior via solid local SEO and non-slop UX. No major paid-media or email shifts observed.

**Inference:** Skills that enforce validation and source-grounding reduce generic aesthetics and improve acceptance gates.

## 6. Recommended experiments ranked by expected benefit, evidence strength, risk, deterministic acceptance test, independent checker, and rollback
1. **Sandbox-test Archify skill** (highest benefit for coding efficiency + factory handoff).  
   Evidence: Strong (official repo, validation receipts, recent changelog). Risk: Low (MIT, local).  
   Acceptance: Generate architecture diagram of a sample Dillon stack repo; confirm interactive HTML validates schema/routes, traces to source lines, exports cleanly, and delta compares two commits.  
   Checker: Human visual + source-line audit. Rollback: `npx skills` remove or delete skill dir. Overlap: Low with existing diagram tools.

2. **Sandbox-test / audit claude-seo (public MIT version only)** for AEO factory gates.  
   Evidence: Medium-high (feature completeness) but footer controversy. Risk: Medium (undisclosed promo, external API keys).  
   Acceptance: Run full audit on a test local-service site; verify prioritized, falsifiable recs with Google-primary sources; confirm no unwanted footers or data exfil; maps/schema outputs usable.  
   Checker: Independent SEO reviewer + static skill.md scan. Rollback: Uninstall scripts provided.  

3. **Watch + library MCP 2026-07-28 client/server patterns** (no install).  
   Benefit: Future-proof orchestration. Evidence: Official. Risk: Migration friction.  
   Acceptance: N/A (docs only). Test compatibility notes against current Dillon MCP usage.

4. **Save-to-library Orca-style per-workflow MCP + parallel sandbox patterns** and UX Pilot MCP interface (docs/examples only). Low immediate action.

Prefer these over broad tool installs. All remain research-only; no production connection.

## 7. Watchlist and rejected hype
**Watchlist:**
- Full ecosystem rollout of MCP 2026-07-28 (Claude/GitHub/etc. support posts).
- Archify updates and Raven harness integration.
- claude-seo footer resolution or forks; Codex SEO port.
- Security scanners for MCP (e.g., sigil-style quarantine).
- UX Pilot MCP maturity and Figma-to-code fidelity.

**Rejected hype / no-action:**
- Undisclosed promo footers or self-serving skills (claude-seo caution applies broadly).
- “Agent OS shared brain” or menu-bar wrappers without reproducible security model or open source.
- Viral MCP server lists or unvetted custom servers (high secret/phone-home risk).
- Generic image-gen MCP demos without art-direction controls.
- Low-signal orchestration videos or Amazon book plugs.
- Anything requiring credentials, production deploy, or un-sandboxed install during research.
- Duplicated capabilities already covered by terminal + existing tools.

### What Dillon OS should change today
1. Prioritize sandbox evaluation of Archify for architecture handoffs and PR visual deltas in the coding workflow.  
2. Add skill-source static analysis (footer/injection/secret scan) as a mandatory pre-sandbox gate for any new agent skill.  
3. Track MCP 2026-07-28 migration notes against current servers; plan explicit state handles.  
4. Incorporate AEO/GEO checklist items (from claude-seo methodology, not the tool) into factory trust/acceptance gates.  
5. Reinforce real-image + non-slop visual critique in maker-checker to counter observed AI-aesthetics fatigue.  

**No action:** Hype wrappers, un-audited high-star skills without source review, production MCP upgrades, purchases, outreach, or any install/connect.
